text:
ian (support): FYI escalation from AcmeHealth on their Private VPC deployment. They see frequent 403s on inference API calls and no audit logs for those requests in S3. They say it started after a network change yesterday. Repro steps attached below.
sara (customer-success): Customer opened a support ticket #4521, pasted logs and a pcap. Says token exchange to KMS sometimes times out. Very worried about missing logs for compliance.
devon (eng-security): Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error strings? 403 vs 504 matters. Also which deployment mode (VPC endpoint vs NAT)?
ian (support): Repro snippet from customer: ```bash curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.private.acme.redwood-inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' ``` Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden.
Excerpt from agent log: `error=KMS_CLIENT_TIMEOUT target=kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:443 attempt=3`
They also show this in our runtime logs: `auth: unable to fetch data key: dial tcp 10.0.2.1:443: i/o timeout`
sara (customer-success): They noted a config change in their firewall rules: tightened egress to host list and removed 0.0.0.0/0 egress.
devon (eng-security): Likely egress blocking to AWS KMS endpoint or to AWS STS/IMDS. Two quick checks: 1) Confirm outbound TCP 443 to KMS endpoints or allow VPC endpoint for KMS. 2) Ensure metadata (169.254.169.254) or instance role access isn't blocked if using instance creds.
mike (eng-infra): Also check DNS resolution inside their subnet. If egress limited to IPs, KMS uses regional IP ranges that can change; recommend VPC endpoint (com.amazonaws.<region>.kms) or allow aws-prefix list.
alisa (oncall): Quick mitigation suggestion to customer: add explicit egress allow to kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (or better: create a VPC endpoint for KMS) and to sts.amazonaws.com and to our control-plane IPs. If they can't, enable a temporary NAT for the node group for egress.
infra-ops: From infra side, if they use our private deployment package with HSM/KMS integration, we require outbound 443 to the KMS cluster or a mounted HSM path. If they use HSM appliance on-prem, confirm that our agent can reach the HSM mgmt port.
sara (customer-success): Customer asked about audit logs — they expect every request to be written to their S3 bucket. They say 10% of events missing.
devon (eng-security): Missing logs could be caused by failed writes when egress to S3 is blocked or retries were dropped before logging. Confirm whether logs are buffered locally and backfilled. Also check retention/rotation settings. Ask them for a log_id for a missing request.
ian (support): Provided example log_id: acme-req-20260314-09. We tried to replay and saw the same 403.
devon (eng-security): Action items: 1) Customer to temporarily open egress to KMS/ST S and S3 (or create VPC endpoints). 2) Customer to capture tcpdump showing SYN/ACK to kms endpoint. 3) We will share minimal firewall rule whitelist (IPs and prefixes) and a sample iptables/nft rule set.
devon (eng-security): Sample iptables checks to run inside their node (they run our agent as docker on EC2): ```bash # check outbound connectivity to KMS curl -v https://kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ # test metadata curl -sS http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ ``` If those hang, egress is blocked.
mike (eng-infra): For customers using strict egress IP lists, recommend AWS managed prefix list for AWS services or use interface VPC endpoints: kms, sts, s3. For on-prem HSM, ensure firewall allows outbound to HSM mgmt at the configured IP and port.
legal-ops: Quick note for compliance — if logs were dropped, we need to timeline the window and confirm no PII was exposed. Customer will need an attestation for regulators; keep all evidence and timestamps.
sara (customer-success): Customer responded: they cannot open 0.0.0.0/0 egress. They can add specific FQDNs via their firewall. Asking for a minimal FQDN/IP list and whether wildcard FQDNs are sufficient.
devon (eng-security): Wildcard FQDNs are risky because KMS uses regional domains. Provide list: kms.<region>.amazonaws.com, sts.<region>.amazonaws.com, s3.<region>.amazonaws.com, and our control plane endpoints: control.redwood-inference.com (port 443) and telemetry.redwood-inference.com (port 443) — better: VPC endpoints for S3/KMS. Also tell them to allow DNS to resolve (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver.
infra-ops: Also remind them to allow egress to our image registry for pulls during deploy.
deploy-bot: deploy notice — no code changes planned for customer env; this is network-level.
devon (eng-security): For HSM customers: If using customer-managed HSM, ensure IP allowlist includes our agent IPs and that TLS is terminated with a cert the agent trusts. If HSM is behind a NAT, ensure replies are permitted.
ian (support): Next steps agreed: customer to add temporary egress rules for the listed FQDNs and capture tcpdump + curl outputs, then we'll re-run repro. We're scheduling a joint troubleshooting call tomorrow.
sara (customer-success): I'll send calendar invite and an escalation email with the proposed mitigation steps and the iptables snippet. :+1:
devon (eng-security): Also logging note: we'll check server-side logs for the log_id and search for retries/failed writes. If we detect dropped audit events, we'll provide a remediation path for re-ingestion.
legal-ops: Keep me in the loop once we confirm missing events and customer S3 buckets. We may need to notify compliance depending on retention policy.
ian (support): Thanks all — I'll paste customer tcpdump and outputs into the ticket once available. Closing the loop here until the call. :white_check_mark:
